sentences.text: Heard Sri. Vageesh N, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Rahul Rai K, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. This petition is filed by the petitioner, being aggrieved by the concurrent findings of the Courts below, the petitioner has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471 and 420 of IPC.
3. The ranks of the parties in the Trial Court will be considered henceforth for convenience.

4. Brief facts of the case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that the Deputy Director of Public Instruction (DDPI)
lodged a complaint stating that a notification was issued for the appointment of 1,800 posts of teacher in the year 1997-98 on merits basis through the District Employment Exchange, Hassan.
The accused during the course of his report before the committee submitted forged SSLC marks card, which is marked as Ex.P.3, with a fraudulent intention to deceive the Authority and to get a job.

During the course of preparation of preliminary list, scrutinizing committee informed their higher officials on suspecting SSLC marks card of the accused stating that the said marks card might be forged.

The Authority referred the said Ex.P.3:SSLC marks-card to A.C.Ranganatha Higher Secondary School where the accused studied, to compare the SSLC marks card along with marks sheets maintained in the school.
5. The School Authority verified marks obtained by the accused with the register of which, it was maintained in the school.
As per the school records, the said accused obtained only 215 marks out of 600 marks.
However, Ex.P3 marks-card discloses that he secured 365 out of 600 marks.
Having confirmed the forgery and fabrication of the marks card, the said DDPI lodged a complaint against the accused.
The jurisdictional police registered a case in Cr.No.211/1999 for the aforesaid offences.

After registering the case, the jurisdictional police have conducted investigation and submitted charge sheet.
6.
To prove the case of the prosecution, the prosecution examined 13 witnesses as P.Ws.1 to 13 and got marked 21 documents as Ex.P.1 to P21.
After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Trial Court recorded the conviction for the aforesaid offences.

Being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence in C.C.No.512/2002 dated 15.06.2012, the accused preferred an appeal before the Appellate Court challenging the validity of conviction passed by the Trial Court.
The Appellate Court after re-appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record dismissed the appeal filed by the accused.
7. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below are perverse and illegal.
Therefore, the same are liable to be set aside.
The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the prosecution has failed to prove the person who forged and fabricated the said document.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that, the defense taken by the accused in the cross-examination has not been properly appreciated.
Therefore, the re-appreciation of the said defense is required to be made.

It is further submitted that, there is no evidence that the accused had produced the said marks-card along with his application or he personally submitted the said application along with the marks-card.
9.

It is further submitted that to constitute an offence under Section 465 of IPC, the prosecution must prove that the accused had personal knowledge regarding the said forgery and he voluntarily forged the said document.
In addition to the forgery, the prosecution invoked Section 420 of IPC.
The prosecution must prove that the accused had knowledge or intention to de-fraud or deceive the Authority to get the job ab-initio.
In the absence of evidence regarding forgery and cheating, the judgment of conviction and its confirmation cannot be sustained.

However, the Courts below failed to appreciate the evidence of all the witnesses and the documentary evidence properly,
consequently, the impugned judgments have been passed which are required to be set aside.

10. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently justified the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below and submitted that the accused with an intention to induce the officials for the purpose of securing the job of primary school teacher, submitted fake marks-card.
11.
It is further submitted that the evidence of all the witnesses clearly indicate that the petitioner had committed forgery and cheating.

Further the prosecution has proved the documents produced by the accused are concocted and fabricated and especially, Ex.P3-marks-card has been tampered by the accused and the same has been fortified through the expert evidence who is examined as P.W.10.
12.
It is further submitted that the accused has not proved that he had not personally submitted the application along with the documents.
Merely because he took the defense that it was submitted by one Chidanand who is working in the Department of Education that may not be sufficient to conclude that he had not submitted the documents.

13. It is further submitted that the Courts below rightly recorded the conviction after appreciating both oral and documentary evidence on record and therefore, it simple imprisonment not appropriate to interfere with the said findings.
Hence, the revision petition has to be dismissed.

14. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the findings of the Courts below, it is appropriate to state the facts in brief and also necessary to have cursory look upon the evidence of all the witnesses in order to assess any irregularities or errors committed by the Courts below in recording the conviction.

15. The briefly stated the facts of the case are that, the accused said to have produced Ex.P.3-SSLC marks-card to secure primary school teacher job and which was notified by the Government of Karnataka for the year 1997-98.
The Scrutinizing Committee while scrutinizing the documents noticed that eight marks-cards of different persons have been tampered and forged, brought it to the notice of the higher officials.

According to her, there are some candidates produced fake documents to secure the job.
Suspecting about the genuineness of the documents of some of the candidates including the petitioner and called them into the hall to ask explanation.

22. P.W.7-Mr.Krishnegowda was working as a Principal in Dathathreya Primary Teachers' Training Centre, Channarayapatna.

29. On careful reading of the evidence of all the witnesses, now, it is relevant to analyze the evidence of all the witnesses stated above.
30. Before adverting to the case of the prosecution, it is relevant to refer the proposition of law in respect of forgery, cheating etc.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Deepak Gaba and others Vs. State of U.P. and another1 paragraphs No.19, 20, 22 and 23 held as under:
"19.

, observed that for the offence of cheating, there should not only be cheating, but as a consequence of such cheating, the accused should also have dishonestly adduced the person deceived to deliver any property to a person; or to make, alter, or destroy,
wholly or in part, a valuable security, or anything signed or sealed and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security.
20.
In the present case, the ingredients to constitute an offence under Section 420 read with Section 415 IPC are absent.
The pre-summoning evidence does not disclose and establish the essential ingredients of Section 415 IPC.
There is no assertion, much less legal evidence, to submit that JIPL had engaged in dishonesty, fraud, or intentional inducement to deliver a property.

It is not the case of Respondent No.2 complainant that JIPL had tried to deceive them, either by making a false or misleading representation, or by any other action or omission; nor is it their case that JIPL had offered any fraudulent or dishonest inducement to deliver a property.
As such, given that the ingredients of Section 415 IPC are not satisfied, the offence under Section 420 IPC is not made out.

22. Section 470 lays down that a document is "forged" if there is:
(i) fraudulent or dishonest use of a document as genuine; and (ii) knowledge or reasonable belief on the part of the person using the document that it is a forged one.
- 13 - Section 470 defines a "forged document" as a false document made by forgery.

23. As per Section 464 IPC, a person is said to have made a "false document":
(i) if he has made or executed a document claiming to be someone else or authorised by someone else;
(ii) if he has altered or tampered a document; or (iii) if he has obtained a document by practicing deception, or from a person not in control of his senses."
31.

On careful reading of the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Co, it makes it clear that,
to record the conviction for the offence under Section 420 of IPC, there should not only be the intention of cheating, but, there is a consequence of such cheating.
32.
Now in the present case, the accused said to have produced forged marks-card and applied for the post of primary school teacher.

Though, he attempted to secure B.K. Manjegowda vs State By Hassan Extension Police on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195151564/
6 the job by producing the fake marks card, he did not proceed further to get the job.

sentences.text: The intention to cheat the person to deliver any property to any person or consent that any person shall retain - 14 - any property has not been fulfilled.
Mere attempting to cheat a person by producing the fake documents cannot be equated to the extent that the act has been completed.
33. On careful reading of the evidence of P.W.4 and P.W.9, the petitioner was not present when they summoned him inside the chamber after having suspected the genuineness of the marks-card.

"Mere production of forged document is not an offence of cheating, unless, the accused is benefited from the said document and moreover, the prosecution has not proved that the said marks-card which is marked as Ex.P.3 was forged by the accused.

Therefore, it can be inferred that the Trial Court and Appellate Court failed to take note of this aspect and recorded the conviction which is erroneous and therefore, the concurrent findings are liable to be set aside.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Revision Petition is allowed.

The judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 15.06.2012 in C.C.No. 512/2002 on the file of II Addl. Civil Judge and J.M.F.C. at Hassan and its confirmation order dated 01.01.2016 in Crl.A.No. 63/2012 on the file of III Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Hassan are hereby set aside.
